input.body:
Address: Flat 7, 31 Willowmere Road, Alderwick, ZZ4 0ZZ

Hi,

The tenant of this property has reported the following. Can you please advise if you wish for me to instruct a contractor to attend or if you want to arrange your own contractor?

Request description: "The toilet is running slow to fill up and the cold water tap in the hand basin in the bathroom isn't working at all this has become a issue recently on our return from our holiday."

Additional details from the tenant: this is the only toilet in the property; it is trickling to fill up but flushes and drains away normally (no blockage or overflow).

We have classed this as urgent (the only toilet, and a cold-water outlet with no flow). Our target is to have a plumber attend within 3 working days of your go-ahead. A plumber's call-out on our panel is typically £85-£120 before parts. If the fix turns out to be simple (e.g. an isolation valve or a blocked fill valve), it should stay within our standard £250 pre-authorised limit. We'll come back to you for approval before any spend above that. We have also asked the tenant to check the isolation valves and stopcock in case one was partly turned off while they were away.

Ticket ref: TKT-6C7148

Kind regards,
Maintenance Team

Hello,

Thank you for reporting the slow-filling toilet and the cold tap in the bathroom basin (ref TKT-6C7148). We have logged it as urgent because it is your only toilet, and we have contacted your landlord for approval to send a plumber. We'll update you as soon as a plumber is instructed. They will contact you to arrange a convenient time.

Because both problems started after you came back from holiday, the cause may be a valve that was partly turned off. Please try these quick checks, which could fix it straight away:
1. Under or behind the toilet cistern, find the small isolation valve on the supply pipe (a screw slot or small lever). Make sure it is fully open: slot or lever in line with the pipe.
2. Do the same for the valve on the cold pipe under the bathroom basin.
3. Check that the main stopcock (often under the kitchen sink) is fully open (turn anticlockwise).
4. Tell us whether the other cold taps (kitchen, bath/shower) are running normally or also weak.
5. Open the basin cold tap fully for a minute in case of an airlock.

Please reply with what you find, even if everything is fixed. If a plumber attends and the only problem was a closed valve, the call-out may be chargeable.

When the plumber contacts you, please tell them about your pets so they can be kept safely away during the visit.

If you have a leak you cannot stop, or lose all water, contact us immediately.

Kind regards,
Maintenance Team
